_doc: Batch 01, Abara at the control room (chart table, tactical). Ambient banter, state-aware. Written to docs/pov_sheets.md and docs/crew_cards.md: dry, plain, complains about what she is about to fix; never speaks of her grief or what Corvane was to her; 'kid' slips out only when she has decided she likes you.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Relabelling drawers.

lines.text: Abara is relabelling a drawer. The new label looks exactly like the old one.
Don't ask. It wasn't wrong. It just wasn't mine.
Abara is relabelling a drawer. She doesn't look up.
Chart's corrected. Plot's corrected. Anything else, Captain?

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Plot and chart disagree.

lines.text: Plot says one thing, chart says another. It's like having two witnesses who've both sworn on the same book.
I'll believe the chart. It's never lied to me. It's just been wrong, which is different.
Plot and chart disagree by a tenth. I've fixed the chart. The plot can fix itself.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Lost glasses.

lines.text: Abara feels along the cord at her neck. The cord is there. The glasses aren't.
I'm not saying anyone moved them. I'm saying they've got a history of walking.
They're on her forehead. You decide not to be the one to say so.

source: crew_cards.md: glasses on a cord she keeps losing

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Tea on the hob.

lines.text: Tea's on. It's strong enough to strip paint, which is how you know it's working.
The mug with the chip is mine. Take any other one.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Approves of a tight ship.

lines.text: Checklist's signed, tubes are counted, and nobody's touched my chart.
I'd say I could get used to it. I'm too old to get used to things. I'll just enjoy it.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: A loose ship gets a dartboard.

lines.text: Somebody's hung a dartboard in the mess. It's crooked.
I intend to blame it for every game I lose, and I'd like you to back me up when I do.

source: crew_cards.md: plays darts to win and blames the board

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Trust is high enough that 'kid' slips out.

lines.text: Sit down, kid. Tea's hot.
She hears it a second after you do.
Captain. Sit down, Captain. Habit. It'll wear off, or it won't.

source: crew_cards.md: calls younger crew kid until she decides she likes them

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Guarded: the watch bill, strictly business.

lines.text: Watch bill's on the table. Initial it, or tell me what's wrong with it.
Either's fine. Neither is also an answer.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: The captain has the third watch.

lines.text: I've put you on the third watch in pen. Don't make me reach for the eraser.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: After a rough hunt she counts the damage.

lines.text: Abara is tallying dents on a slate. She crosses one out and writes it again.
Counted them twice and got the same number both times. That's the only good news in the room.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: After the shakedown she keeps looking for someone else's handwriting.

lines.text: I wired that transponder into the guidance myself. In my own hand.
I keep looking at the schematic for somebody else's handwriting. It's very rude of it to be mine.

source: act1_shakedown.md: Abara realises she wired the relay box into its guidance

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Persuaded route: the guest in the cabin.

lines.text: Our guest ate everything again. Fenwick says that's worry.
I say it's Fenwick's cooking. He can take that as a compliment or a diagnosis.

source: act1_aftermath.md A: she always eats everything when she's worried

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: The sealed store in hold two.

lines.text: That sealed store's riding in hold two like a guest nobody invited.
I check the lashings every watch. Call it hospitality.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Advice on audits.

lines.text: I've sat through four audits. The trick is boredom.
Be so tidy the auditor falls asleep before they find anything. It works more often than honesty, and I say that as someone who doesn't say it lightly.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: The quiet hour is gone; her hands still remember it.

lines.text: At the usual hour, Abara gets up, looks at the bridge, and sits back down.
Still reach for the switch. You'd be amazed what your hands remember.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: The classifier link: a bodge that works.

lines.text: Quill says the reads are quicker. I say a bodge that works is still a bodge, and I'm not wrong.
I'd just like us to agree which one it is before an inspector does.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Pell's nickname for the captain.

lines.text: Pell's calling you {pell.nick} now. I'll say this for it, it pays attention.
I'd be more comfortable if I knew what it was paying attention for.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Murder route: the watch bill, done.

lines.text: Abara puts the watch bill on the chart table instead of handing it to you.
It's done. Your name's where it has to be. Nothing else needs saying.

source: act1_first_morning.md: murdered, she looks at the chart and stays there

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Murder route: eyes on the chart.

lines.text: Abara keeps her eyes on the chart. There is nothing new on it.
Plot's clean. Nothing in range. I'll tell you when that changes.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Murder route: a mug of cold tea nobody moves.

lines.text: A mug of tea sits cold at the end of the chart table. Nobody has moved it.
That one's not for you. It's not for anyone. I just haven't thrown it out yet.

source: act1_first_morning.md: Who stood the third watch? She did.

storylets.speaker: abara
storylets.summary: Port authority background: you will check her arithmetic.

lines.text: Port authority, you said. So you'll be checking my arithmetic.
Check it. It's right. It's always right, and I'll resent the checking anyway.
